 3 MVC No.712/2022  JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 09-12-2021 at about 7.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as cleaner in Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-41-C- 5886, driven by its driver from Bengaluru to Tumkur,
carefully, by following all the traffic rules.

When the petitioner reached Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 highway road, near Sharapura Palya Gate, Nelamangala Taluk, at that time the driver of the Tata Ace bearing No.KA-53-C-5294 came from same direction, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without following the traffic rules and suddenly drove the same from the right side to left side.
Due to which, the Canter in which the petitioner was traveling dashed to Tata Ace vehicle.
Due to the said impact, the Canter fell on the road and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Harsha M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025
Indian

Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/
2 took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein
he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as cleaner and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said TATA ACE, for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18%
per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 3 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.3 has filed its written statement.
The respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied involvement of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C- 5294 in the alleged accident and the manner in which the accident has taken place.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the present petition.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C- 5886 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, on the date of the accident.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 was not at all responsible for the cause of accident, as the driver of the said Tata Ace was moving slowly, cautiously and on the correct side of the road.
As such this respondent is not a necessary and proper party for the adjudication of the above petition.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the canter bearing Reg.
No.KA- 41-C-5886 drove the same, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without maintaining safety distance in between the vehicles and in the process of overtaking the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the rear portion of the moving Tata Ace vehicle and thereby caused the accident.

Further it is contended that, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the rear portion of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C- 5294 is damaged and front portion of the canter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-5886 is damaged.
Hence, it is clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the canter.

The said sequence of events clearly establishes that, the driver of the Tata Ace has been wrongly/intentionally implicated by the Police in the charge-sheet as accused No.1 and the obvious intention is to fasten the liability against the respondent insurance company by taking advantage of the policy of insurance.
Hence, there cannot be any liability against this respondent insurance company as driver of the Tata Ace vehicle was not at all responsible for the cause of the accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 in favour of respondent No.2 and it was valid for the period from 06-12- 2021 to 05-12-2022.

Further it is contended that, the owner of the Tata Ace bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-C-5294 has willfully entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not had a valid and Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/
3 effective driving licence to drive the same on the date of the accident and as such the respondent No.2 is guilty of breach of the terms and conditions of the policy and as a result of the same this respondent is not liable to indemnify the insured and accordingly the above petition is liable to be dismissed against it.
It has seek protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 09-12-2021 at about 7.00 a.m., near Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 highway road, near Sharapura Palya Gate, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.

What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.
Further, he has got examined two more witnesses namely E. Selwyn Jebasing and Dr. S.A. Somashekara as P.W.2 and P.W.3 respectively.
On the other hand, the respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:

10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazer and sketch, Ex.P.4 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.6 is true copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.7 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is discharge summary, Ex.P.10 are medical bills (total 54), Ex.P.11 are advance receipts (total 4), Ex.P.12 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.13 is x-ray,
Ex.P.14 is authorization letter, Ex.P.15 is MLC extract, Ex.P.16 is case- sheet, Ex.P.17 is OPD slip and Ex.P.18 is x-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 and suddenly moving the said vehicle from right side to left side of the road, without giving any indication.
Due to which, the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-41-C-5886, which was proceeding in the same direction, got dashed to the rare portion of offending Tata Ace vehicle.
Due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and left hand.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8,
has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294.
12.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C- 5294 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.3 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1 and insurance policy holder/respondent No.2, as they did not choose to contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.3 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Eicher Canter bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-5886, as he was driving the same without holding valid driving licence, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and in the process of overtaking the Tata Ace vehicle lost Sumanth R. 5 control over his vehicle and dashed against the rear portion of the moving Tata Ace.

Further it is contended that, at the time of accident, the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53- C-5294 was driving slowly, cautiously and on the correct side of the road and there is no negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
But, the respondent No.3 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any oral evidence or produced any documentary evidence to establish the above contentions.
Even, the respondent No.3 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 and suddenly moving the said vehicle from right side to left side of the road, without giving any indication.

Due to which, the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-41-C-5886, which was proceeding in the same direction,
got dashed to the rare portion of offending Tata Ace vehicle.
Due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left leg and left hand.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-C-5886 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
13.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 30 feet wide Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 Highway road, infront of Sri Lakshmi Srinivasa Agro Foods Flour Mill, near Sharapura Palya Gate, Nelamangala Taluk, in between the offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C- 5294 and the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-41-C-5886, in which the petitioner was travelling.

sentences.text: Further, it is not the case of respondent No.3 that, the accident in question has taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the said accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing No.KA-41-C- 5886, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.8 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 in the said accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary,
Ex.P.13 x-ray, Ex.P.15 MLC extract, Ex.P.16 case-sheet, Ex.P.17 OPD slip and Ex.P.18 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has suffered post traumatic fracture shaft of left femur.
The same is deposed by P.W.3, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.

On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.3, to show that, the above Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/
6 medical records are false documents.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: 17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 09-12-2021 at about 7:00 a.m., on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 Highway road, infront of Sri Lakshmi Srinivasa Agro Foods Flour Mill, near Sharapura Palya Gate, Nelamangala Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained post traumatic fracture shaft of left femur and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
As per Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 04-05-2000.

The accident has taken place on 09-12-2021 at about 7:00 Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/
7 a.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 22 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered post traumatic fracture shaft of left femur.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 37% physical disability of left lower limb and 18% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.7 Wound certificate, Ex.P.9 Discharge summary, Ex.P.13 X-ray, Ex.P.15 MLC extract, Ex.P.16 Case- sheet, Ex.P.17 OPD slip and Ex.P.18 X-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injury and he has undergone surgery for the said injury.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 09-12-2021 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 01-09- 2023, which is after lapse of one year and nine months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that,
P.W.3 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture sustained by the petitioner is united and alignment is normal.

Further he has clearly stated that, there is no loss of muscle tissue,
it is not an open fracture, there is no external wound, there is no infection, no deformity and no complication at the fracture site.

Further, he has clearly admitted that, as the petitioner is aged about 22 years the union of fracture will be fast and physiotherapy treatment will be given for mobilization and improvement of range of movements.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as cleaner and was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was working as cleaner and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2021.

ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 54 medical bills, as per Ex.P.10.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the bill at serial No.49 is not in the name of the petitioner.
Therefore, the said bill is not taken into consideration.
Hence, the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.87,670/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.87,670/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury i.e. post traumatic fracture shaft of left femur.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days from 09-12-2021 to 15-12-2021, in K.I.M.S. Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 22 years and unfortunately he has suffered post traumatic fracture shaft of left femur.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.30,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,88,800-00 2.
Medical expenses 87,670-00 3. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 7,000-00
5. Food and nourishment 5,600-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 5,000-00 7. Loss of income during 30,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses 20,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,34,070/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is the policy holder and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.
The insurance policy bearing No.773222123340001427, issued by the respondent No.3, in respect of vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 53-C-5294, was valid from 06-12-2021 to 05-12-2022,
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer Sumanth R. Gowda vs Bheema on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84708719/
10 under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the driver of offending vehicle by name Raghavendra S/o Mallappa was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA-3320130001946 and it was valid from 02-04-2018 to 01-04-2038 and the offending vehicle was insured by respondent No.3 insurance company and it was valid from 06-12-2021 to 05-12-2022.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-53-C-5294 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,34,070/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-),
from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.3, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,34,070/- (Rupees six lakh thirty four thousand and seventy only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
